---
title: "Did mobile crisis authorization change the ED time gap?"
---

CMS approval dates, SPA effective dates, and statewide operational launch dates are not interchangeable. Some SPA effective dates are retroactive, and CMS approval does not establish when qualifying teams operated statewide. [CMS approval announcement](https://www.cms.gov/newsroom/press-releases/cms-approves-new-hampshires-request-provide-essential-behavioral-health-services-through-mobile).

The exploratory group-time ATT analysis uses SPA effective dates as an intention-to-implement treatment. The event study reports pre-period diagnostics as well as post-policy estimates. Event time zero is +3.1 minutes (state-cluster bootstrap 95% interval −9.2 to +15.7); the earliest four-state cohort (AZ, NC, NY, OR) is −16.9 minutes at event time zero and −18.8 at event time two, with wide intervals that include zero. These estimates are not evidence of an effect or no effect.

An approval-date sensitivity analysis shifts timing later. Event times zero and two have only two treated states each, so their intervals are especially unstable. Neither timing specification measures when mobile-crisis services actually became available statewide. See the [full method and limits](../results/mobile_crisis_policy_analysis.md), [effective-date event study](../results/mobile_crisis_event_study.csv), [approval-date sensitivity](../results/mobile_crisis_event_study_approval_date.csv), and [treatment-date audit](../policy/mobile-crisis-adoption.csv).
